SoftBank’s November 10 restructuring of U.S. data-center turbine reservations and Erste Group’s November 18 downgrade highlight heightened sensitivity to any cooling in hyperscaler power commitments heading into 2027. Meanwhile, the Wind division’s $400–$500 million 2026 EBITDA loss and execution risks around financing and closing the $9.0 billion Trench Group acquisition (half debt-funded, closing late 2027) leave little room for operational stumbles while technical momentum stays negative.
cons: Shares sit in a sharp technical breakdown at $699.33, trading well below all key moving averages on elevated selling volume.
Erste Group downgraded GEV to Hold on November 18, warning that 2027 new-order growth is set to moderate against rich valuation multiples.

en.fundamental: GE Vernova sits at the physical power bottleneck of AI infrastructure through heavy-duty gas turbines and high-voltage grid equipment. On October 28, 2026, Q3 results beat expectations: revenue rose 27% year-over-year to $12.64 billion, adjusted EBITDA reached $1.9 billion (15.4% margin), and GAAP EPS hit $4.81. Power ($6.07 billion revenue, 21.4% EBITDA margin) and Electrification ($3.86 billion, 19.1% margin) carried growth, while Wind turned slightly positive in Q3 ($72 million EBITDA) but still carries a $400–$500 million full-year loss outlook. Orders jumped 96% organically to $29.3 billion, pushing backlog to $197 billion (122 GW in gas commitments). Management raised 2026 revenue ($46.5–$47.5 billion), EBITDA margin (13.5%–14.5%), and free cash flow ($16–$17 billion) targets, doubled buybacks to $20 billion, and agreed to buy Trench Group for $9.0 billion. The gas-and-grid moat remains intact.
en.headline: GE Vernova Plunges Below Key Averages Despite $197B Backlog and Third Guidance Raise
news: October 28, 2026 — Q3 2026 earnings beat expectations as revenue grew 27% YoY to $12.64 billion, organic orders surged 96% to $29.3 billion, and backlog hit $197 billion. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for a third time (free cash flow to $16–$17 billion) and doubled its share buyback authorization to $20 billion.

October 28, 2026 — GE Vernova agreed to acquire high-voltage grid equipment maker Trench Group from Triton Partners for $9.0 billion (funded evenly with cash and debt). Expected to close in late 2027, the deal adds 11 plants and roughly $5 billion in backlog to the Electrification segment.

November 10, 2026 — SoftBank disclosed a $3.73 billion charge via Silver Bands 7 LLC after scaling back excess power-equipment procurement for U.S. AI data centers in Ohio, forfeiting $2.85 billion in non-refundable deposits. GE Vernova stated there was no direct financial impact on its business, though shares dropped over 6% on sector-wide AI capex worries.

November 17, 2026 — GE Vernova launched HYpact-145g, a compact 145 kV switchgear free of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) designed for space-constrained high-voltage substations, expanding its grid modernization lineup.

November 18–20, 2026 — Erste Group analyst Hans Engel downgraded GEV from Buy to Hold on November 18, citing expected 2027 order-growth moderation, high valuation multiples, and slow Wind recovery. Shares subsequently plunged 7.53% to $699.33 on November 20 amid a broader sell-off in AI-linked power stocks.
en.opportunity: The sharp sentiment reset contrasts starkly with GE Vernova’s expanding multi-year visibility. With $197 billion in backlog, gas-power commitments approaching 130 GW by year-end 2026, and grid-component scarcity reinforced by the Trench Group deal and November 17 HYpact-145g SF6-free switchgear launch, earnings durability extends well past near-term market jitters. Moreover, customer slot down-payments driving $16–$17 billion in projected 2026 free cash flow and an enlarged $20 billion buyback authorization give management substantial capacity to absorb share volatility once selling pressure and stretched technical indicators stabilize.
en.opportunityCheck: The page’s AI-opportunity profile is largely well calibrated, especially its strong credit for bottleneck pricing power—confirmed by SoftBank forfeiting non-refundable deposits and GE Vernova’s $16–$17 billion 2026 free cash flow forecast driven by customer slot down-payments. However, the AI revenue exposure score looks slightly too low and warrants a modest upward revision: Power and Electrification already generate nearly 78% of Q3 revenue, while data-center demand propelled a 96% organic order surge to $29.3 billion and the $9.0 billion Trench Group deal deepens grid leverage. Meanwhile, market growth is appropriately tempered by expected 2027 order moderation.
pros: Q3 2026 orders jumped 96% organically to $29.3 billion, lifting total backlog to $197 billion and gas-power commitments to 122 GW.
Management raised 2026 guidance for the third time on October 28, projecting $16–$17 billion in free cash flow and doubling buybacks to $20 billion.
The October 28 agreement to buy Trench Group for $9.0 billion vertically integrates scarce high-voltage bushings, transformers, and $5 billion in grid backlog.
SoftBank’s $2.85 billion forfeited deposit on November 10 highlighted GE Vernova’s strong contract protection and pricing power in gas turbines.
risks: Decelerating 2027 order momentum if hyperscalers delay or resize AI data-center power buildouts, as hinted by SoftBank’s procurement revision.
Persistent losses in the Wind division, still guided for $400–$500 million in full-year 2026 EBITDA losses.
Integration, regulatory, and debt-financing risks from the $9.0 billion Trench Group acquisition, which is not expected to close until late 2027.
Valuation multiple compression in high-beta AI infrastructure equities during broader risk-off macro environments.
en.summary: GE Vernova (GEV) slid 7.53% to $699.33 on November 20, 2026, capping a 41.5% pullback from its $1,195.94 52-week high. The sell-off followed SoftBank’s November 10 disclosure of a $3.73 billion power-procurement charge and Erste Group’s November 18 downgrade to Hold over 2027 order moderation. Yet core fundamentals accelerated in Q3 2026 (October 28), with orders surging 96% organically to $29.3 billion, backlog reaching $197 billion, and full-year free cash flow guidance raised to $16–$17 billion. Technicals are firmly bearish, while the long-term turbine and grid moat stays intact.
en.technical: GE Vernova’s chart as of November 20, 2026 shows a clear bearish breakdown. At $699.33 (down 7.53% on the day), price sits well beneath all three exponential moving averages (EMAs, which track average price trend over 50, 100, and 200 trading days): EMA 50 at $872.56 has already crossed below EMA 200 ($889.22), while EMA 100 remains at $911.14, signaling steep intermediate-term deterioration. Momentum confirms the sell-off: MACD (12/26/9, a trend-momentum gauge) stands at -44.34 below its -37.84 signal line with a -6.50 histogram, indicating persistent downward pressure. RSI 14 (a 0–100 momentum gauge where under 30 is oversold) fell to 31.98, nearing oversold territory without yet signaling a reversal. Volatility is stretched, with price closing beneath the lower Bollinger Band (a 20-day volatility channel spanning $709.27 to $926.67, midpoint $817.97) and resting in the bottom quarter of its $530.16–$1,195.94 52-week range. Volume hit 6.20 million shares—39% above the 4.47 million 20-day average—confirming heavy institutional selling. Immediate resistance sits near $709–$745 and $818, while the 52-week low at $530.16 anchors distant structural support.

th.summary: GE Vernova (GEV) ดิ่งลง 7.53% ปิดที่ $699.33 เมื่อ 20 พ.ย. 2026 รวมปรับฐานแล้ว 41.5% จากจุดสูงสุดรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ที่ $1,195.94 แรงขายถูกกดดันจากข่าว SoftBank บันทึกค่าใช้จ่าย $3.73 พันล้านจากการปรับแผนจองอุปกรณ์ไฟฟ้า (10 พ.ย.) และ Erste Group ลดคำแนะนำเป็น Hold (18 พ.ย.) เพราะกังวลคำสั่งซื้อปี 2027 ชะลอตัว อย่างไรก็ตาม ปัจจัยพื้นฐาน Q3 2026 (28 ต.ค.) ยังแข็งแกร่ง คำสั่งซื้อโต 96% แบบออร์แกนิกสู่ $29.3 พันล้าน แบ็กล็อกแตะ $197 พันล้าน และปรับเพิ่มเป้ากระแสเงินสดอิสระเป็น $16–$17 พันล้าน ภาพเทคนิคเป็นขาลงชัดเจน แต่ป้อมปราการธุรกิจระยะยาวยังมั่นคง
th.technical: กราฟเทคนิคของ GEV ณ วันที่ 20 พ.ย. 2026 อยู่ในภาวะขาลงชัดเจน ราคาปิด $699.33 (-7.53%) อยู่ต่ำกว่าเส้นค่าเฉลี่ยเคลื่อนที่แบบเอ็กซ์โปเนนเชียล (EMA — ตัวชี้วัดแนวโน้มราคาเฉลี่ย 50, 100 และ 200 วันทำการ) ทั้งสามเส้น โดย EMA 50 ($872.56) ตัดลงต่ำกว่า EMA 200 ($889.22) แล้ว ขณะที่ EMA 100 อยู่ที่ $911.14 สะท้อนการอ่อนตัวรุนแรงในระยะกลาง ด้านโมเมนตัม MACD (12/26/9 — ตัวชี้วัดแรงส่งของแนวโน้ม) อยู่ที่ -44.34 ต่ำกว่าเส้น signal (-37.84) พร้อมค่า histogram ติดลบ -6.50 ชี้แรงขายยังต่อเนื่อง ส่วน RSI 14 (มาตรวัดแรงซื้อขายช่วง 0–100 หากต่ำกว่า 30 ถือว่าขายมากเกินไป) ลงมาที่ 31.98 ใกล้เขต oversold แต่ยังไม่เกิดสัญญาณกลับตัว ราคาปิดหลุดกรอบล่างของ Bollinger Bands (ช่องความผันผวน 20 วัน ช่วง $709.27–$926.67 เส้นกลาง $817.97) และอยู่โซนล่าง 25% ของกรอบ 52 สัปดาห์ ($530.16–$1,195.94) วอลุ่มพุ่ง 6.20 ล้านหุ้น สูงกว่าค่าเฉลี่ย 20 วันที่ 4.47 ล้านหุ้นราว 39% ยืนยันแรงเทขายหนัก แนวต้านระยะสั้นอยู่แถว $709–$745 และ $818 ส่วนแนวรับสำคัญระยะไกลอยู่ที่จุดต่ำสุด 52 สัปดาห์ $530.16
